title: Lesson 90: Final Synthesis: The Enterprise AI Architect's Toolkit, Complete
description: Tests the four-shelf toolkit sort, the difference between a capability limit and an enforced control, the seam that explains an unapproved action, and the rule for choosing two deep areas as an accountable architect.

questions.question: An architect must tell the difference between a capability limit and a control. Which item is a control?
options: A prompt line that tells the agent never to send email to a customer
A deny rule that blocks the send tool entirely
A named on-call owner recorded in the runbook
A quarterly re-label of the held-out evaluation set
questions.explanation: A capability limit is an instruction the model reads and can decline on a given run, while a control holds regardless of what the model decides. A deny rule that blocks the send tool is enforced outside the model, so it is a control.

questions.question: An action is capped at draft-only so a human must approve every send, but unapproved sends keep occurring. Where is the real permission set?
options: In the autonomy rung recorded in the design document
In the evaluation set that scores the action after the fact
In the credential scope that the tool actually runs under
In the governance policy approved by the review board
questions.explanation: A bounded autonomy rung does not bound an action if the credential behind it can write. The scope of the service account is the real permission, and it is usually set somewhere the design document never mentions.

questions.question: An architect is choosing the two areas to go deep on. What rule applies when she is accountable for a system already in production?
options: One of the two areas must come from the control shelf.
Both areas must come from the shelf with the nearest failure.
The two areas must be the newest protocol and the newest tool.
Both areas must come from the build shelf.
questions.explanation: Deep areas are picked by exposure and visibility, then constrained by accountability: one of the two must come from the control shelf, because that is where generalist knowledge becomes expensive. A deep area without an artifact within thirty days is only a reading list.
